title: Windowed Restore & Disaggregated Prefill Controller for Burst-Aware KV Restore
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: under bursty traffic and mixed-tenancy we observe long-tail prefill stalls when restoring KV pages into GPU memory. The current prefill is monolithic and often contends for bandwidth with decode microbatches, causing higher p95 token latency and increased tail cost.

Goal: implement a disaggregated prefill controller that restores KV pages using time-windowed, priority-aware restore lanes and a soft-reservation hierarchy. The controller will: (1) split prefills into short 'fast' windows for critical prefixes and longer background windows for opportunistic restores; (2) expose soft reservation slots for canary/cold-tenants to reduce noisy-neighbor restores; (3) integrate with kernel selection heuristics so that kernels which tolerate partial KV presence can be preferred when a full restore is delayed.

Scope: design and implement the controller, a priority queue for page restores keyed by prefix utility, eviction feedback hooks (softly delaying evictions for ongoing restores), and a small evaluation harness to measure p50/p95/p99 token latency and token-cost delta across synthetic burst patterns.
acceptance_criteria: Controller can run as an independent scheduler task on a serving shard and accept restore requests via existing prefill RPCs
Fast-window restores complete < 4ms for hot prefix pages in 95% of cases under burst load (internal benchmark)
Integration test demonstrating kernel fallback when a full KV page is missing, with no correctness regressions
End-to-end regression tests for eviction-feedback preventing double-restore races
Performance dashboard (Console) tile for restore queue depth and lane utilization published to runtime-1.25 staging
design_notes: Prefill lanes: fast (high utility, short window), normal (regular), background (low priority, preemptible)
Utility estimation: combine recent touch frequency, token-span weight, and decoder cost impact estimate from profiler traces
Soft reservations: allocate fractional slots per tenant class (e.g., enterprise:0.6, free:0.1) that can be borrowed under low utilization
Backpressure: if restore queue grows beyond horizon, throttle low-utility background lanes and prefer kernel variants that use KV-on-disk fallback
Eviction feedback: eviction requests mark pages as 'in-flight' for X ms to allow restores to complete; eviction metrics feed into compactability scoring
implementation_plan: Week 1: design review + proto API for restore lanes and queue metadata (PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/2207)
Week 2: implement scheduler loop and lane admission control, unit tests for queue semantics
Week 3: integrate kernel hinting path and implement eviction-inflight flag + race tests
Week 4: benchmark harness (burst patterns) and dashboard wiring, rollout to canary nodes
Week 5: gather telemetry, iterate on thresholds, promote to staged rollout for runtime-1.25
metrics: p50/p95/p99 token latency for requests hitting paged-attention
restore queue depth (per-lane) and average wait time
restore success ratio within fast window
token-cost change (tokens GPU time / tokens served) measured in test harness
kernel-fallback rate when prefills are incomplete
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: soft reservations could be gamed by noisy tenants. Mitigation: add adaptive decay and tenant-level credit accounting
Risk: new scheduler introduces extra CPU overhead. Mitigation: keep scheduler per-shard and optimize hot path in C++; measure extra CPU and cap worker threads
Risk: rollback complexity if eviction races remain. Mitigation: feature gate with opt-out, and fast-path to disable background lanes
Risk: incorrect utility estimator causes mis-prioritization. Mitigation: start with conservative weights and A/B test with telemetry sampling
rollout_strategy: Canary rollout to 5% of serving shards with synthetic burst load and heavy telemetry export
Metric thresholds for automatic rollback: p95 increase > 5% or kernel-fallback rate > 2x baseline over 10m window
Escalation path: revert flag, open rollback PR, notify on-call runtime and SRE
test_plan: Unit tests for queue ordering, lane admission, and soft reservations
Integration tests with kernel hinting simulating partial KV availability
Chaos test: force eviction race and verify eviction-inflight semantics prevent double-restore
Performance test: synthetic burst generator replicating production token bursts and mixed-tenant ratios
End-to-end smoke in staging with runtime-1.25 canary before production rollout
